svg.text: Network Firewall — zonal egress before NAT
FORWARD → Read steps 1–5 from left to right
The instance SG permits a new
RETURN ← Start at step 6 on the right; follow steps 6–10 back to the source
IGW delivers the reply to the
endpoint. Use dedicated route tables per AZ. Endpoint
subnet local routing completes the return.
Network Firewall does not supply the NAT Gateway
function. SGs are stateful; NACLs are stateless. Passing
stateless inspection is not automatically a stateful
allow. Track addresses before and after NAT separately.
Inspect firewall flow/alert logs, NAT metrics and route
tables. Check both SYN and SYN-ACK on the same
stateful path. Failure tests must cover endpoint
readiness, AZ loss and SNAT port pressure.
REFERENCES — full clickable source links and validation commands are in the companion Markdown report.
Illustrative addresses • logical service hops • blue = initiating traffic • green = response • control-plane notes are not packet hops
